subdomain: 6.4 Document architectures and provide implementation guidance

en.question: Release 12 of a Claude service changes its tool response schema and retrieval metadata format; release 11 cannot read either new format. A receiving team's rollback runbook says only to redeploy the previous application image. The last accepted release-11 data snapshot and tool version remain available, and a safe manual fallback is approved. What guidance should replace the incomplete rollback step?

options.text: Document and rehearse restoring a compatible accepted application, prompt, tool, and retrieval bundle, with verification, named authority, and fallback if restoration fails.
options.note: The known incompatibilities require restoring and validating the relevant dependencies, not just the application image, under an owned recovery procedure.

options.text: Restore the previous application and prompt while retaining the newest retrieval data and tool service, then monitor users for compatibility complaints.
options.note: The scenario states that release 11 cannot read the newer formats, so this combination predictably fails before user monitoring can validate it.

options.text: Switch to the previous model identifier and leave the application, tool schema, and retrieval metadata unchanged to minimize rollback work.
options.note: Changing only the model does not restore the previous accepted application behavior or address the documented dependency incompatibilities.

options.text: Redeploy the previous image and temporarily disable response validation, using the current data and tool responses until the incident is resolved.
options.note: Disabling validation does not make incompatible formats readable and removes a check precisely when recovery needs verified compatibility.
